name: CO-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Denver-based district with a +29 Democratic partisan lean
Democrat Melat Kiros has raised over $1 million with heavy outside support; Republican Christy Peterson has raised about $2,000
Prediction markets price the Democratic candidate near 98% to win
Open seat after Diana DeGette lost renomination, but the seat's partisanship dominates
model.rationale: This Denver district's +29 Democratic lean makes a Republican win implausible, and the resource gap is extreme: Kiros has out-raised Peterson by roughly five hundred to one and drawn substantial outside spending on both sides. Markets price the Democratic candidate at about 98%, consistent with the fundamentals.
model.watch: A surprise would require a major late scandal or an unusually low-turnout electorate, neither of which is currently indicated.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Diana DeGette (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
This open Denver-area House seat is one of the most Democratic-leaning districts in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 29 points toward Democrats. Longtime incumbent Diana DeGette is not on the ballot after losing renomination, but the seat's underlying partisanship remains the dominant force in the race.

Democrat Melat Kiros has raised more than $1 million and attracted significant outside spending from both supporting and opposing groups, while Republican Christy Peterson has raised only about $2,000. Prediction markets give the Democratic candidate roughly a 98 percent chance of winning. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on the district's fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Democratic hold in the mid-to-high twenty-point range.
